text.p: Daniel Janssen, chief executive officer of Belgian chemicals group Solvay SA, reiterated on Friday the company hoped 1996 current earnings would be in line with those of 1995.

"I can only restate what we said in July...we hope that 1996 current earnings will be of the same order of magnitude as last year," Janssen told a news conference on the group's planned 14 billion Belgian franc sale of its animal health business.
Janssen said the sale to American Home Products Corp, which is subject to approvals, should net the group a capital gain in 1996 of around six billion Belgian francs.
Janssen said the key to Solvay's performance in the second half remained the state of the German economy, particularly the construction sector -- a big user of the group's plastics.
"It's improving and we have increased our prices of all three plastics but still there's uncertainty about what will happen at the end of this year in Europe...due to the economy," Janssen said.
